message: A JWT is decoded without checking its signature (or allows alg 'none'), so anyone can forge a token with any claims.

title: get_sql_profile executes arbitrary SQL with no security validation
reason: The get_sql_profile tool runs the model-supplied sql directly on a pooled connection without auth_context, so DorisConnection.execute skips validate_sql_security; `DROP DATABASE prod` or `GRANT ...` runs as the configured DB user (root by default), bypassing the blocklist that exec_query applies.
fix: Run security_manager.validate_sql_security(sql, auth_context) before executing (or reuse execute_sql_for_mcp), accept only a single SELECT statement, and connect with a read-only Doris user.

title: Metadata tools paste table_name/db_name into SQL string literals, bypassing the SQL validator
reason: get_table_comment (and get_table_schema / get_table_column_comments / get_db_table_list, same pattern at lines 454, 604, 1354, TABLE_SCHEMA = '{db_name}') build information_schema queries with f-strings and execute them via connection_manager.execute_query without auth_context, so no validation; table_name `x' UNION SELECT secret FROM other_db.t -- ` returns any data the root DB user can read, including tables the validator blocks.
fix: Use placeholders: execute_query(session, 'SELECT ... WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = %s AND TABLE_NAME = %s', (db_name, table_name)); validate identifiers with ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ where they must be inlined (USE, SHOW INDEX, DESCRIBE).

title: exec_query relies on a keyword blocklist while connecting as root
reason: The only guard on the run-any-SQL tool is a sqlparse keyword/regex blocklist that inspects only the first parsed statement and misses Doris statements not on the list (e.g. SET GLOBAL, ADMIN ..., SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE), while the default DB user is root; a blocklist is not a working guard for this tool.
fix: Connect the MCP server with a dedicated read-only Doris user (SELECT privilege on the allowed databases only), reject inputs with more than one statement, and allow-list statement types (SELECT/SHOW/DESC/EXPLAIN).

title: HTTP transport binds 0.0.0.0 with all authentication disabled by default

evidence.quote: enable_token_auth: bool = False  # Enable token-based authentication (default: disabled)

reason: The Docker/start script runs Streamable HTTP on 0.0.0.0:3000 and, with token/JWT/OAuth all off by default, authenticate_request returns an anonymous context, so anyone who can reach the port can call exec_query / get_sql_profile against the root DB connection.
fix: Default to 127.0.0.1, refuse to start the HTTP transport on a non-loopback address unless an auth method is enabled, and enable token auth in docker-compose.

title: All MCP request headers, including Authorization, logged at INFO
reason: Bearer tokens sent in the Authorization header are written to the log file on every MCP request, so anyone with log access can replay them.
fix: Drop this log line or redact authorization/cookie/x-api-key headers before logging.
